transcript: Trophy Boys by Emmanuelle Mattana is a searing look at feminism, privilege, and the gender binary. As the debate team of four boys at a private high school prepare for their senior year championship debate, their assigned topic and position stuns them, threatening their winning streak and unraveling a series of hilarious and troubling ideas. What starts as a funny portrait of blind entitlement takes a turn, and things go from theoretical to alarmingly tangible. The way that these actors, none of whom are cisgender men, navigate the tone shifts is really impressive, and furthered by Danya Taymor's sharp and creative direction. Though I had mixed feelings about the way this play concluded, there was one very memorable moment near the end that I thought was a masterful synthesis of writing, direction, and casting, and added a profoundly unexpected layer to an already impressively layered piece. Trophy Boys is running at MCC through July. With that, another program for my collection.
